reasoning: For _fused_moe_kernel, compute utilization is 91.95% (sm__throughput) and roofline Compute SOL is 91.9%, while DRAM throughput is only 42.14% of peak; this indicates arithmetic throughput limits performance rather than memory bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: Heavy non-tensor vector ALU workload from fused FC1+SiLU+FC2 reductions dominates execution.

evidence.interpretation: SM pipelines are close to saturated, leaving little compute headroom.

fixes.fix: Rewrite inner products to use MFMA/tensor-core-style matrix fragments (or Triton dot paths that lower to matrix instructions) and pack data to supported low-precision formats.
fixes.rationale: Current tensor activity is zero, so shifting work from VALU reductions to matrix engines can raise effective FLOP throughput and reduce VALU bottleneck pressure.

root_causes.cause: Kernel is instruction-dense due to repeated scalar/vector ops inside nested TOPK × INTER_DIM × MODEL_DIM loops with dequant and scaling in-loop.

evidence.interpretation: Very high dynamic instruction count indicates instruction throughput pressure in the fused loop body.

fixes.fix: Reduce per-iteration instruction count by hoisting invariant scale/address calculations and increasing K/J tile reuse (autotune BLOCK_J/BLOCK_K and unroll strategy).
fixes.rationale: Lower instruction overhead per output element improves IPC under an already compute-saturated regime.
